purpose: Ripretinib is used to treat a type of stomach and intestinal cancer called gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). It is specifically used when other treatments have already been tried and stopped working. This medicine helps slow or stop the growth of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Cancer cells often have abnormal proteins called kinases that tell them to grow out of control. Ripretinib works by blocking several of these abnormal proteins, including ones called KIT and PDGFRA, which are commonly found in GIST tumors. By blocking these signals, the medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or fatigue, hair loss, nausea, stomach or belly pain, constipation, muscle or joint aches, skin rash or hand-foot skin reaction (soreness, redness, or peeling on palms and soles), decreased appetite, and high blood pressure.
warnings: This medicine can raise your blood pressure, so it will be monitored regularly. It may cause heart problems, including a condition that weakens the heart muscle. Rarely, it can cause a serious skin reaction or bowel problems like perforations (holes in the intestine). It can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is important during treatment and for some time after. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, chest pain, severe stomach pain, or vision changes.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose and it has been more than 8 hours, skip it and take the next one at your regular time — do not double up.
